item.title: manandearth, October 2026
item.description:
This newsletter is about figuring things out and making mistakes along the way.

The idea to start a blog and a newsletter is haunting me this last year. A year like no other. I was prompted to start writing and to double up my reading due to reckoning with life and its flip side. I am not on social media and at the same time I spend a lot of time online, working, writing code and prose, and reading. I invite you to subscribe to this newsletter. It is a patient medium that rests in your mailbox and is a tribute to that part of the internet and of society where our thoughts are(were) ours and we reach(ed) out to find like-minded free thinking, individuals, rather than trends. I intend to publish monthly. I will try, with humility, to provoke some thinking and inspire creativity. The intention is to work around a topic, the content: a story, pen drawings, and black and white photos. There will be references to the external inspiration as well as to related work on my site (follow the links to read the related blog posts and view the images), and if I am favoured by the gods of the internet, the audience will grow and this kind of work will be in demand. Only time will tell. I will also include some work that you could print with future issue.

item.title: Roadkill and tipping
item.description: I go out with my camera looking for a picture, half the time I come back not having taken one shot, the other half I either took a shot in the last light out of desperation, took the last shot a minute before something worth shooting showed up, missed an opportunity because my mind was elsewhere, or took a really good shot, but forgot to set the aperture, or left the cap on, or forgot to turn the film holder around, or... When I finally develop I might find that both negatives in a film holder were loaded on the same side, or the fixer was not good anymore, or I forgot to account for the film being pushed or pulled by a stop, or the negative is solid white or solid black. Seems like there's an infinite number of errors to commit as I keep committing new ones.

item.title: fountain transformation
item.description:
I'm feeling that I reached my limit with ballpoint pens, or at least for now. I am fully submerged in black permanent ink. Three fountain pens by nib size and a Kuretake brush pen all feeding from the one ink pot. The limit, by the way, I meet regularly. Sometimes because I lack the instructions, yet sometimes it is precisely the instructions that show me the door.

A few years ago I became fascinated with cornets. It was before Christmas in Durham, staying with my inlaws. The freezing December wind from the North Sea, the jazz records my father in law played, the smell of coal burning, the street brass bands, I was swimming in horns. In a second hand shop I spotted an old beaten up cornet, so I decided to buy it and have a go. On the bus on the way home, the crowd possesed by the Christmas spook were encouraging our children as they tried to blow a sound out of the old metal tube to no avail. The instrument was finally passed to Martha, then three, and she blew a perfect rumbling C and the crowd cheered.

item.title: Cars
item.description:
1. Sleep

He used to call him Matsli'ah, not a common name, it was his family name and a rather strange one to be honest, in hebrew it means succesful. Never have I met another Matsli'ah before or after this one. In later years he called him by his first name: Itsik.

I only ever saw him in a short period when I was around five or six, in the late seventies, like all my dad’s friends he had a large uncombed mane and largeness in general. Being that young, most people seem large. His flat felt untidy and well lived in. The seventies specialised in cosiness, and that place, the moustached crowd, the coffee, and constant smoke were perfectly that.

item.title: Still going
item.description: There is a story I was telling, one I retold many times yet I haven't told it for a while. Now, getting back to telling the story I've noticed some gaps that I did not know how to fill, and I was getting this odd feeling: `perhaps this never happened?`. I then stopped and reminded myself that I don't make up such stories, that I have no reason to, and that I find enough interest and weirdness in reality not to come up with lies. Well, here is the story:

item.title: livestock
item.description: Ever since veterinary laws were enforced, being since joining the EU, or since the government of one party or the other made keeping pigs condemnable, they are hidden. Pigs run so deep here, if they can't be kept legally, they will have to be kept illegally. I once wanted to create a surveying interactive map of livestock for this little village, a tool to keep stock. every house has a concrete or stone made structure, usually three of four sections divided by walls and a tin roof for pigs. these days mostly I find one sow in each house, or a sow and her son or daughter being fattened up. In my map the pigs will last most of the year, and in the spring a few little ones will join for a short while, then distributed. The turkey population will also be seasonal, and steady, it is the chickens that are the most volatile. although some old hens are steadfast and last and as long as they lay they are safe. The soup made from an old hen is named `old rags`.

item.title: Reorientation
item.description: Every once in a while we change the orientation of the living room table. It's a busy table; to move it on its axis by 90 degrees requires some tidying and sorting first. Some of the objects that are on the table might be totally out of place when reoriented. When I spot them I put them aside to avoid the breach.A lot depends on the success of the operation, if we get it right a new space will be gained, a new era will have begun. So yes, I had enough, something had to be done and to take a real shape, so that it could not be denied. And now all hopes are up, and I have accomplices too; I find it easy to get family members implicated. I am not sure if that is a general rule for families but they do tend to jump into things with me. Perhaps I am very convincing, or too sure of myself, or really bad at expressing my doubts. The bench was moved against the window and the table turned, the spaces around had to be equalized, and the curtains drawn. Of course, every situation has its advantages. We can now relax into this one. We said it was only a try, but not one of us is strong enough to bear another transition. We will settle now, and in a few months, or a year or so, find this stagnation unbearable enough to provoke another quarter of a turn. How many revolutions the table took already? we lost count.

item.title: pinhole
item.description:
The first four images were taken on a Baby Speed Graphics. A 3d printed mount with a hole pierced into foil as a lens, and 9x12 Fomapan cut in a dark bag as the negative. The handmade crude hole jointly with the prevailing winds, and the dusty environment give those prints the hazy dirty look. These are minutes long exposures.

The last photo is a 4x5 negative in a 3d printed box with a more precise hole. Same wind and somewhat less dust.

item.title: Abejarruco
item.description:
Very pleased with my new 55mm lens. Capturing less details, but more fits in. This is winter sun in this latitude. It has its harshness, nonetheless this is exactly what punctuates everything with high contrast.

The rain was long gone but the earth finds it difficult to drink it all just yet. Some of this humidity will have to be shared by evaporation. Like many country landscapes anywhere this nature appearing from the path is thin. The trees might be tall but they hide large fields which are the greater reality of the countryside. In those areas where the field meets the public path, thanks to low maintenence, and municipal priorities we get some overgrowth, and with it what once was the rule.

item.title: Ink characters
item.description: I really don't know where those characters appeared from. When they first crossed my pen, each and every one, I found them embarrassing. They seen to suggest what I did not want to suggest, what I never meant to say. And it is not that by that they uncovered some truth I was trying to conceal, they surprised me with their naive inadequacy. Going through them again after more than a year, they also seem incomplete, the artist impatient, the technique half arsed. Well, enough with that, they are what they are.

item.title: Relevancy
item.description: His name on the screen; the phone on silent mode. It occurs quite often when the phone is on silent: he calls, and I happen to look at the screen and see his name. Curiously, his profile picture is a computer-generated image of two beings embracing, a blue icy male figure and a fiery woman figure. A passion contrasting the word 'Dad' above the image. I click to answer and say "hello dad", his voice more wakeful than I expected, "Hi, listen, I don't know where I am exactly. It is dark here, must be underground... I hear water running. I know it is a hospital, must be the cellar". "is there no one to ask?" I asked, "no" he answered.

item.title: Retention
item.description:
I didn't think I'll end up speaking about myself. I wanted to speak out my mind, and to find connections between the things I do, but consciously or even deliberately speaking about myself has no value, unless it helps relating to others, or communicate to others something beneficial. uff... language, a tool and a barrier.

That is actually what gives the name and the tone to this post. I've been studying French, mostly alone. mostly with books. I started by spending the first 15 minutes of the day with the old and tested method of Assimil. The idea is to keep going, and as long as one goes, and as long as one is not challenged otherwise, the going is good.

item.title: News bias
item.description:
Sometimes I find that I give advice that I didn't know I had. It happened yesterday. My daughter said she is overwhelmed by the news, that she is reading too much, and that it affects her badly. I said that she should be critical about what she reads: What is real news: something that happened, and what is just some sensationalist piece of distraction: something that someone wants you to hear, or wants someone to hear. Noise. Some of the problems with populism is that it is insincere, it is loud, and it doesn't care about truths. It is there to win, and no price is too high.

The language of art and the language of speaking about art are on a different level, and I think that it can communicate in a way that is especially important. “Really observing”, “really noticing”, which unlike scientific observation, it is creative observation, it creatively exposes, intelligently exposes, so it can suplement science. Art is consumed by way of attention, actively unlike the attention given as a passive spectator of a television show or an online video post. Art is written in a language both familiar and cryptic, we need to create the space and quietness to tune in.

item.title: Mountain Ink
item.description: I used to draw from references, but this year I've started drawing from imagination. I realised that there is so much recorded in my head, that I don't need to look at in order to imagine completely. There is quite a way to go still, I mostly can't say that I am happy with the drawings, but the issue isn't proportions or correctness of details and shading, mostly the issue is that I don't understand where those images came from, some of them are right down embarrasing, all of them are strange, more about that later, in this letter I will say goodbye to some drawings made with references, either photograps I took, or photographs in books.

item.title: Things you see from here, you don't see from there
item.description: Is this the point where a socialist turned into an anarchist? Did this just happen? I never gave it much thought really. I guess that I thought Anarchy is just utopian, like all its critics do, thinking it is probably not going to work, which is besides the point, as no other system has proven to work, certainly not the current one. I'll start at that moment, or the moment just before: I was running up a hill. A hill that I run almost daily. It is not an easy climb, but I am used to it, and my mind busily wanders and then.. I am at the top before I know it. I was thinking, not sure what about. The voice in my head was judging and calling one opinion 'mature', and demanding therefore that opinion to be accepted, being close to 'objective' and 'correct' and 'true'. Yet surely there is no objective point of view and whatever idea depends perspective, on a point of view, as well as on context. What we call 'mature' represents a so called 'mature' point of view, and is not free from an interest in a specific outcome.

item.title: Simancon
item.description: This is not going to be easy. The subject is a series of underexposed photos on the top of Simancon. Going up there this time, we were overtook by a few runners, mostly solitary, but there was at least one couple as well. Every time we are there I think that perhaps if I lived there this would have been my daily run. The village below lays at about 900m above see level and the peak is at 1,549m, so it's fairly a serious daily jog. I wonder how fast it could be done if one get's into the rhythm of doing this daily.

item.title: Scratchy cut film
item.description: Part of the magic of taking photos in black and white is due to the fact the photographer doesn't naturally see in black and white. The results are surprising even before all the possible errors in exposure and the variables inherent in the chemical process. We humans don't see the world in monochrome. This and the fact that we read the world in colors, and black and white film does not; all those greens and reds and blues reduced to a grey soup. It makes for challenging and strangely rewarding medium.
